title: Grilled Reuben Sandwiches for the Crew
displayTitle: Grilled Reuben Sandwiches for the Crew
seoTitle: Grilled Reuben Sandwiches for the Crew | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Reuben night—corned beef char on the griddle, rye pressed crisp for ten
subtitle: Grilled corned beef, sauerkraut, Swiss, and rye for ten
description: Thick-cut corned beef grills on the flat-top until charred, stacks on rye with sauerkraut, Swiss, and Thousand Island, and presses until melty and crisp.

steps.title: Warm sauerkraut
steps.instruction: Drain sauerkraut and warm in a small pan at 140°F with pinch of caraway. Hold warm. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat the flat-top griddle
steps.instruction: Preheat griddle to 425°F for beef, then reduce to 375°F for pressing. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill corned beef
steps.instruction: Grill thick corned beef slices 2 minutes per side until charred edges and warmed through. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold beef
steps.instruction: Hold grilled corned beef covered at 170°F in hotel pans. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build reubens
steps.instruction: Spread Thousand Island on rye. Layer Swiss, corned beef, sauerkraut, more Swiss. Butter outer rye. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Press sandwiches
steps.instruction: Press reubens at 375°F 3 minutes per side until rye is crisp and cheese melts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold wrapped
steps.instruction: Hold finished reubens wrapped in foil at 170°F up to 20 minutes. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Line for ten
steps.instruction: One reuben per firefighter with pickle chips on the side. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Drain sauerkraut well—wet kraut steams bread instead of crisping.
Thick-cut corned beef survives the press; deli-thin shreds.
Caraway in warmed kraut adds classic reuben aroma.
tonightSpread: Grilled reuben sandwiches with pickle chips.
Potato chips or dill pickle spear.
leftovers: Corned beef hash with sauerkraut next morning.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Reubens feel like deli night at the hall. Corned beef grills fast on the griddle, holds at 170°F, and presses in minutes between calls.
mealPrepNotes: Grill corned beef slices at 425°F, 2 minutes per side. Hold at 170°F up to 30 minutes. Press reubens at 375°F, 3 minutes per side.
